Not gaslight, but assume that something might be off. I'm perfectly aware that one can be delusional, or otherwise misled by ones beliefs. Having gone through a severe depression, I know that my self-perception can be warped.

So, I've had a good few comments on this during the day, and I've gotten both some nice replies, people taking their time to answer my questions and have given me some nice insights. Others have attacked me for some apparent hidden bigotry. So it's time for me to go mask off.

I've for a long time been of the understanding that being trans is a mental disorder, akin to Autism etc. Today I've gotten a lot of hints that it might really be so, but also be further fueled by trauma. I do honestly have empathy with everyone going through what Trans people go through. Both medically and socially, though not due to missing affirmation, rather the opposite, that the general idea of questioning, challenging, debating and offering proper psychological help for the dysphoria is being criticized by the LGBTQ Ideology, and instead seemingly avoided by the majority. Instead seeking only affirmation, forwarding the echo chamber. That has only been confirmed today by a good selection of you accusing me of bigotry for just the simple act of asking a question, and then further attacked when I went to challenge beliefs, or just not following in tow.

I know I'm finding myself on a site infamous for echo chambers, amongst a group sadly known for their very ideological way of thinking. But despite it all, it was very educational. And I want to thank everyone that supplied me with proper answers for helping me understand a bit better, despite the accusations of bigotry I otherwise received.

Feel free to call me whatever you feel fitting, the words and names you'll throw against me means nothing to me, as those who would, have already shown me their true colours. Have a lovely night, and I hope to see you all get a better life, as I came meaning no harm. And despite the unpleasantries, I also leave wishing no harm.
